newsitem.title: MEXICO: Last Mexican septuplet dies after 6-week struggle.
newsitem.headline: Last Mexican septuplet dies after 6-week struggle.

text.p: A baby boy who had been the only surviving member of Mexico's first septuplets died on Sunday after battling for nearly six weeks against chronic heart problems, his doctor said.

"All hope for (his mother) Maria del Rocio Diaz has vanished," Dr. Eduardo Torreblanco said in a report issued by the Mexican Social Security Institute. "The last of the septuplets born on Jan. 21 died this morning."
The cause of death at 2 a.m. local time (0300 EST) on Sunday was the failure of Fernando Fabian's heart to respond to treatment, the medical report said.
Prior to his death his weight had fluctuated around 2.2 pounds (1 kg), and doctors had warned of grave danger of either lung, heart or brain failure.
Two of his sisters died last weekend from a string of problems emanating from the premature multiple birth. Three other siblings perished within the first two weeks of birth.

The septuplets, five girls and two boys, were born 12 weeks early during the first pregancy of their 28-year-old mother, who had used fertility medicine after trying unsuccesfully to get pregnant for five years.
The parents had repeatedly expressed hope that at least some of their children would survive. Their father, 29-year-old Fernando Morales, said it was "a miracle" when they were born.
